primary-metric.purpose: The strongest number on the compact menu overview, using rounded system typography and stable digits.

settings-primary-metric.purpose: Today’s local total in the available-width Settings overview; paired with its token breakdown and scaled down when needed.

motion.name: numeric-update
motion.purpose: Makes changing token totals legible without turning them into decoration; disabled for Reduce Motion.

motion.name: refresh-turn
motion.purpose: Confirms that refresh began; disabled for Reduce Motion.

motion.name: status-fade
motion.purpose: Softens status-label changes; disabled for Reduce Motion.

narrative.overview: CodeRim should feel like a compact macOS instrument that is ready when opened and disappears when the user returns to work. It is precise, calm, and native: the first screen answers the immediate questions, while charts, projects, sessions, and full limit details remain one click deeper. The product uses system materials, semantic labels, SF Symbols, hairline separators, and tabular numerals instead of decorative dashboard chrome. Density is intentional, but every section must have one clear purpose and retain enough spacing to scan quickly.
keyCharacteristics: Native macOS controls and semantic system styling.
Token totals remain the strongest visual signal.
Progressive disclosure instead of one long provider dashboard.
Quiet status communication with explicit text for warnings and estimates.
Motion explains change and never blocks interaction.

rules.name: The Semantic Color Rule
rules.body: Do not replace native semantic colors with fixed light- or dark-mode values.

rules.name: The Text-With-Color Rule
rules.body: Warning and critical colors always appear with an explicit label such as “Low” or “Critical.”

rules.name: The Number Stability Rule
rules.body: Use monospaced digits and numeric content transitions anywhere changing values could shift the layout.

rules.name: The Usage Viewport Rule
rules.body: Settings owns one outer ScrollView for both the overview and its available-width detail destinations; content starts at the top and scrolls when the window is shorter than the content. Do not add a second popover-sized scroll region inside Settings. The compact menu retains its separate content-fitting, height-limited detail viewports.

rules.name: The One-Question Rule
rules.body: Each destination answers one question: limits, usage, projects, or sessions.

rules.name: The Real-Provider Rule
rules.body: Token Usage is the cross-source token summary. A named provider limits tab appears only when that provider has working data and status handling; empty provider tabs are not navigation.

rules.name: The Notch Content Bounds Rule
rules.body: The tooltip shell, placement, pointer region, and session budget use the same content-height calculation, including Today, the account row, named limit groups, and their spacing. Natural text must fit inside the card before its mask is applied; grouped rows receive their spacing once. Preserve the existing notch silhouette, ring geometry, palette, and motion while adapting the tooltip height to its content.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Use tonal grouping and system materials before introducing custom elevation.

rules.name: The Native Control Rule
rules.body: In the Settings window, do not redraw a platform control solely to mimic another app. (The notch is the deliberate exception — it is Codenotch's language, not this one.)

dos: Do keep Token Usage focused on token totals and history, and Codex Limits focused on account limits and reset timing.
Do use semantic system colors, SwiftUI text styles, SF Symbols, VoiceOver labels, keyboard shortcuts, and Reduce Motion.
Do show unknown or incomplete cost data as unavailable in detailed analytics instead of zero.
Do keep local token totals, account-wide profile totals, quota percentages, and API-equivalent estimates visibly distinct.
Do add Claude, Gemini, or another provider behind a shared provider boundary before exposing it in navigation.
donts: Don't copy CodexBar branding or assets; reuse only mode separation and information-architecture ideas that improve scanning for CodeRim's real features.
Don't place charts, projects, sessions, credits, every provider, and every limit on the overview.
Don't show empty or speculative provider tabs.
Don't use purple/blue AI gradients, neon, decorative glass, giant cards, or custom dashboard chrome.
Don't communicate low quota, stale data, or estimates through color alone.
